hints: Look closely at time X and compare the solid ventricle line with the dashed aorta line. Which one has just become higher than the other?
Remember valves open when pressure behind them is higher than pressure in front, and think about what the atria do while the ventricles are contracting.
walkthrough:
**Read the pressure lines at time X**

Look at the graph at X. The solid ventricle line is shooting steeply upwards and has just risen above the aorta line.

At the same moment, the dotted atrium line is very low and falling:
$$P_{ventricle} > P_{aorta}$$

**Decide the aortic semilunar valve action**

Valves always open in the direction of high to low pressure. Because ventricular pressure is now greater than aortic pressure, blood is pushed out into the aorta.

So the aortic semilunar valve is opening, not closing.

**Decide what the atrium is doing**

At time X, ventricular systole is starting. The atria are relaxed in diastole and blood from the vena cava and pulmonary veins is flowing in to fill them.

The low atrial pressure shows the atrium is not contracting and emptying, it is filling. That gives opening + filling.

options.A: Closing is wrong because ventricle pressure exceeds aorta pressure, so the valve must open. Emptying is wrong because the atrium is relaxed and collecting blood.
options.B: Filling of the atrium is correct, but closing of the aortic valve is wrong. High ventricular pressure opens this valve to allow ejection.
options.C: Opening is correct, but emptying is wrong. Atrial systole has just finished, so the atrium is now in diastole and filling.
options.D: Correct. Ventricle pressure rises above aorta pressure so the aortic semilunar valve opens, while the relaxed atrium fills with venous blood.
